title: DINOv3 multi-dense-task compressed Mirror head bank
native_method: DINOv3 (Meta 2025) frozen high-quality image patch features, Gram anchoring and native linear or Mask2Former segmentation decoder; official segmentation and depth heads are meaningful controls
hypothesis: After source-family learning of one shared dense readout basis over frozen DINOv3 features, learned m can replace much of the stored per-task decoder state while preserving useful independent segmentation/depth/normal outputs; cheaper simple native linear decoder basis is mandatory null.
shared_physical_object: one unmodified frozen DINOv3 ConvNeXt-Tiny or ViT-small feature pyramid evaluated once for each image; task decoder family for semantic classes, depth bins, surface normals or cloud masks
mirror_insertion: tiny task/scale-specific Mirror m operating in shared dense feature/readout basis with separate **paid** output-shape projection per task; not a rotation of incompatible semantic outputs
fixture: CPU 16×16 synthetic images with geometric shape segmentation labels, depth ramps and oriented normal regression; 4/5 independent target tasks with overlap alpha in {0,.5,1}; 128 source scenes, 256 dev, 512 fresh, whole scene-grammar split. Use one shared 32-channel 4-level feature encoder; no pretrained-image claim. Natural stage pinned DINOv3 ConvNeXt Tiny and four real dense-label domains with scene/site-disjoint splits.
implementation_steps: 1. Verify official frozen DINOv3 multi-layer features and original linear/Mask2Former decoder exactly. 2. Train native per-task decoder and DPT-style depth head under allowed source/task budget, no Mirror. 3. Learn a source-only common feature decoder dictionary and tiny task m (sign/Householder/Givens/diagonal) with task-specific final linear map and units declared. 4. Compare full native outputs, ordinary same-byte low-rank/tensorized heads, one shared trunk K independent native linear heads, task-conditioning FiLM, and proposed m+private residual. 5. Evaluate spatial heldout scenes, segmentation boundaries, depth ranking and normal angles; count all image encoder/decoder bytes and actual single-backbone calls.
native_and_simple_controls: DINOv3 original frozen backbone with independently trained native linear segmentation/depth heads
Native DINOv3 Mask2Former and dense decoder when official runnable
Shared feature pyramid with ordinary K linear readouts (single encoder forward)
Same-byte rank-k/tensorized low-rank native head dictionary, FiLM and IA3
Independent task decoders and a full per-task fine-tuned backbone as upper reference
Random feature code, shuffled task labels and segmentation-only ablation
measurements: segmentation mIoU/Dice, depth AbsRel/RMSE, normal cosine/angle (rad), worst task, genuine extra function diversity, total model+head bytes, GPU/CPU P50/P95 and actual backbone calls
compute_resources: CPU synthetic first; official DINOv3 code and licensed pretrained checkpoints required for natural; e.g. ConvNeXt Tiny to fit limited GPU; record license and pretrained hash.

gates.PASS: In >=4/5 fresh disjoint scene worlds, preserve task quality within <=0.02 mIoU or +0.02 relative depth RMSE of best native one-backbone multihead, reduce paid task-decoder payload >=20% with <=1.10x P95 and a Pareto win over ordinary equal-byte decoder basis.
gates.FAIL: Native shared-backbone independent heads are faster/more accurate at same bytes, m only moves a semantic class color/coordinate without improving heldout prediction, feature normalization/preprocessing differs across methods, or dense native decoder GPU dominates.
gates.UNCERTAIN: native unverified, missing performance data, contaminating test data or threshold uncertainty spans zero

counterexample: DINOv3 already supports frozen single-backbone multipurpose predictions, so one heavy vision forward itself is not new. Task-specific output geometry varies; code may only compress a small head while baseline encoder dominates physical storage.
uncertainty: Class imbalance, spatially correlated pixels and scenes, geometry-specific target units, image patch resolution and augmentation leakage. Bootstrap by whole scene and sensor domain.
